page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is a general-purpose virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, the server offers 2 vCPUs backed by 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It features dedicated CPU allocation, 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB per core. The instance has no local storage included and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced single-core execution alongside constrained multi-core performance. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1842.18, and the single-core Geekbench score measured 1556.0, placing single-thread capability in average performance brackets. However, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 1815.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 1932.39 due to its single-core physical topology. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 15.1 GB/sec for reads and 13.63 GB/sec for writes, which limits high-throughput memory operations.

Given its core topology and hardware configuration, the ecs.g7se.large delivers moderate resource density for light compute workloads. The inclusion of hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AES vector extensions enhances cryptographic and vector-processing execution. Workloads requiring high multi-threading or intensive database operations show reduced throughput, with Redis SET operations yielding 1.97 million operations per second and database performance scoring low. Consequently, the instance is best suited for entry-level general-purpose workloads, lightweight web services, microservices, and single-threaded batch execution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.large is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, paired with 8.0 GB of memory and a 1 Gbps network baseline. Hardware specifications include 48 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support, with no local storage or GPUs attached. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates average single-core performance, achieving 1842.18 in single-core stress-ng tests and 1556.0 in Geekbench single-core testing. Multi-threaded performance and memory bandwidth show reduced results due to the single physical core topology. High-frequency memory write bandwidth reaches 13.63 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 3.5 GB/sec. The instance provides a cost-effective environment for low-density workloads, lightweight application servers, microservices, and single-threaded processing tasks.
